phase: Performance Batch 2A: Demand production profiling (measurement only, no optimizations implemented, no production code committed)

methodology.approach: Per-phase in-process measurement at production-representative scale on the canonical 59,096-segment Fifth Ring partition + synthetic points/data at the production chunk scale (~500k rows/chunk). Pure-function benchmarks are not sandbox-blocked.
methodology.why_not_full_run: The full 12 GB / 90.1 M-row Demand run could NOT be executed: the sandbox boundary guard blocks Demand stage runs on non-tiny fixtures (verified blocked: 120 k-order run, 5 k-order run on the canonical partition; allowed: 3-order tiny run). The full run would take ~70 min and peak ~11 GiB and is certainly blocked.
methodology.scale_note: Spatial-index build cost depends on the segment layer (59,096 segments), not the order count, so per-call STRtree costs are production-real. Point/nearest/sqlite/gzip costs are measured at representative scale and extrapolated to the 500 k-chunk / 90 M-row / 180-chunk production aggregate. Post-staging SQL passes over 46 M rows (ordered SELECT, GROUP BY, export JOIN) and the 413 MB POI read are GB-scale and remain unmeasured.

spatial_matching_breakdown.measurement: match_points_to_segments_with_distance, 250,000 points x 59,096 segments, 3 calls, median

point_construction.mechanism: Python list comprehension [Point(xy) for xy in zip(...)] + GeoDataFrame construction

spatial_index_build.mechanism: seg_view.sindex STRtree build (rebuilt every call: sindex_rebuild counter = 1 per call; seg_view is a fresh slice so the index is NOT reused across calls)

sindex_reuse.note: The STRtree IS rebuilt every call (fresh seg_view slice), but the build cost is only 0.6% of spatial matching -- NOT the bottleneck.

spatial_matching_breakdown.key_finding: STRtree build is NOT the spatial bottleneck. The static-audit hypothesis (Batch 0 B2) that STRtree rebuild dominates is DISPROVEN by measurement. Point construction (the Python Point() list comprehension) dominates at 80%.

per_phase_measured.note: single streaming pass over 46M rows; SQL JOIN scan is separate (unmeasured)

per_phase_measured.scope: pd.read_csv chunk of the 12GB orders CSV

per_phase_measured.note: LOWER BOUND: benchmark table had no PRIMARY KEY; production staged_orders has stage_id AUTOINCREMENT PK -> later appends slow as the PK index grows (degradation unmeasured at GB scale)
Python loop only; the ordered SQL SELECT (ORDER BY driver,time over 46M) is separate and unmeasured
negligible; do NOT continue optimizing DEM-02

build_cluster_od_from_staging SQL GROUP BY over 46M rows (uses idx_staged_slot_od)

per-chunk DataFrame overhead (.copy x3, to_numeric, boolean masks)

stage_level.cpu_utilization: single-core (no multiprocessing anywhere in src/; the pipeline runs stages in isolated child processes)
stage_level.peak_rss_estimate: ~11.2 GiB (production record); the dense OD tensor (1.59 GiB) + SQLite staging (peak ~GB, deleted after) + POI (0.4 GiB) are the contributors
stage_level.filesystem_read_bytes_estimate: ~12.5 GB (12 GB orders + 413 MB POI + 17.8 MB partition + 43 MB relations)
stage_level.filesystem_write_bytes_estimate: ~5 GB outputs (orders_region_assigned.csv.gz 2.69 GiB + cluster_od 606 MB + od_tensor npz + graph assets) + SQLite staging peak (deleted)
stage_level.sqlite_peak_size: unmeasured at GB scale (sandbox-blocked); staged 46M rows x 14 cols, estimated GB-scale
stage_level.per_chunk_degradation: sqlite_append expected to slow as the DB grows (stage_id AUTOINCREMENT PK index updates) -- mechanism confirmed, magnitude unmeasured at GB scale; spatial_index_build cost is constant across chunks (constant 59k-segment layer, no degradation)

ranking_by_measured_wall_time.phase: UNMEASURED SQL passes + POI graph (prime suspect for the 70m total)
ranking_by_measured_wall_time.evidence: gap = 70 - 26 measured; requires full-run to confirm

next_batch_recommendations.title: Vectorize Point construction (shapely/geopandas points_from_xy) instead of the Python [Point(xy) for xy in zip(...)] list comprehension
next_batch_recommendations.evidence: Measured 80% of spatial matching (~17.5 min extrapolated). The STRtree-reuse hypothesis is disproven (sindex build is 0.6%); do NOT pursue sindex caching as the primary fix.
next_batch_recommendations.risk: low -- no tie-break or row-order change (same Point geometries); determinism-safe. Must verify sjoin_nearest result is byte-identical.

next_batch_recommendations.title: Measure the full production Demand in an unguarded environment with the enhanced timing to quantify the post-staging SQL passes (ordered SELECT / OD GROUP BY / export JOIN)
next_batch_recommendations.evidence: The measured phases sum to ~26 min vs the 70 min production wall; the ~44 min unmeasured gap is in the GB-scale SQL passes, which are the prime suspect for the true 70 min driver. This must be confirmed before committing to SQLite-side optimizations.

next_batch_recommendations.title: Conditional on DEM-P2: if the SQL passes dominate, test SQLite transaction batching / prepared-statement append / sharded staging; if Point construction is confirmed, implement DEM-P1
next_batch_recommendations.evidence: Decision per the measured ranking; do not optimize DEM-02 further (od_tensors is 0.15 min).
next_batch_recommendations.risk: medium for SQLite changes (staging ORDER BY + GROUP BY are load-bearing for carpool labeling and OD aggregation; any rewrite must preserve the driver/time/stage_id sort and the GROUP BY semantics)

conclusions: The static-audit STRtree-rebuild hypothesis (Batch 0 B2) is DISPROVEN: STRtree build is 0.6% of spatial matching; Point construction (Python Point() list comprehension) is 80%.
Spatial matching is the largest MEASURED phase (~21.6 min extrapolated), but is NOT the sole 70 min driver -- ~44 min remains in unmeasured GB-scale SQL passes.
od_tensors is negligible (0.15 min) -- do NOT continue optimizing DEM-02.
The full production run is sandbox-blocked in this environment; the enhanced timing (in the working tree, env-gated, uncommitted) is ready to run in an unguarded environment to close the 44 min gap.
No optimizations were implemented; no production code was committed (the profiling timing enhancements stay uncommitted in the working tree per the task constraint).
